content.text:
Only Rb5Au3O2 (mp-29920) fits the observed pattern; no second phase is needed.

1. **Observed peaks.** The main peak is at 28.85° (intensity 100). Weaker peaks sit at about 20.15°, 28.2°, 29.95°, 30.75°, 39.0°, 43.35°, 50.5°, 53.5° and 59.7°.
2. **Candidates ruled out.** Seven candidates fail because their peak pattern near the main peak is wrong:
   - TaCrO4, KV4O10 and LiEu2IrO6 each have two or more comparably strong peaks there. The observed pattern has one dominant peak.
   - SrLaCoO4 has a second peak at about 63% intensity next to its main one. Nothing that strong is observed.
   - NaLa(WO4)2 has a peak of about 31% at roughly 18.2°. The observed pattern shows only noise there.
   - Li7SbO6 has strong peaks below 20° that are not seen.
   - LaY3Sc4O12 is a perovskite-type cell, so its main peak should fall near 31.5°, not 28.85°. I estimated that position from the cell rather than reading it off the simulation.

   I did not locate LiVO2's peak positions exactly, but its strong reflections are not in the observed list.
3. **Indexing Rb5Au3O2.** Using its orthorhombic cell (a = 5.795, b = 7.529, c = 14.582 Å), each observed peak lands within about 0.2° of a computed reflection:

   | Observed (°) | Reflection | Computed (°) |
   |---|---|---|
   | 20.15 | (111) | 20.25 |
   | 28.2 | (120) | 28.26 |
   | 28.85 | (121) / (104) | 28.92 |
   | 29.95 | (023) | about 29.95 |
   | 30.75 | (122) / (200) | 30.83–30.85 |
   | 39.0 | (220) | 39.2 |
   | 43.35 | (007) | about 43.35 |
   | 53.5 | (321) | about 53.5 |

   Its simulated pattern shows the same features: a single dominant peak with a small peak just below it and two stronger ones above. I did not assign the 50.5° and 59.7° peaks individually. Some intensities also differ, for example about 42 simulated versus 23.5 observed for the peak near 30.7°.

{"present": ["mp-29920"], "confidence": 0.8, "note": "Main peak 28.85 deg and peaks at 20.15, 28.2, 29.95, 30.75, 39.0, 43.35 and 53.5 deg index well on the Rb5Au3O2 cell; other candidates' strongest peaks are absent."}
